derivation:
1759. The original corridor pivots of the physical mean: exact row derivative, normalization, and pullback to the full fine-exterior chart. This computes the selected fluctuation variables rather than replacing them by a rank-selected minor or by target elimination.

UNCHANGED DATA. Hold fixed the same original fine torus, group G, fine exterior F,V0, actual active coarse row set I, chosen physical M_fix (either CMP109(0.4) OR (0.12), never a mixture), physical reference U0, original density, cutoff, beta_ref/g1_ref, and all other constraints. The raw independent fine orientations form E. Use the source's centered physical blocks B(y) of odd L>11, not the older anchored auxiliary gauge blocks. The actual source selected bond beta(c)=b0(c) is the fine bond contained in the coarse straight path c and in its corridor B(c)={b: b_- in B(c_-), b_+ in B(c_+)}. With h=(L-1)/2 and c:y->y+L eta e_mu, its lifted endpoints are y+h eta e_mu and y+(h+1)eta e_mu. Periodic paths are read on their source lift and projected with their oriented link occurrences. The same original geometry is used, not a replacement torus.

Before eliminating these ORIGINAL pivots one must verify in the actual instance that the beta(c), c in I, are distinct independent original fine variables and belong to E minus F. This input does not certify the actual sector's I/F/support dictionary merely from notation. It does not permit replacing a fixed beta by another convenient pivot. Native auxiliary roots or tree edges need not coincide with these physical pivot variables.

LITERATURE BINDING. CMP109 pp.252-254 (0.3)-(0.12) defines the centered blocks, endpoint paths, translated straight middle paths, and the physical means. CMP109 p.267 (after (2.10)) defines b0(c) by the corridor, h supported on those bonds, and LQh=I; (2.4) on p.266 identifies the actual relative physical mean before the linearization. CMP119 p.249 removes the delta constraints by solving the variables A'(b0(c)), retaining C, background dependence, sigma, determinants and z^(0). Those displays do not already audit the actual physical K_C or identify every old relative-mean propagator Q with the physical derivative below.

GEOMETRIC SUPPORT AND EXACT ROW DIAGONALITY. Every endpoint path Gamma in G(y,x), x in B(y), stays within that ONE centered block. It never uses any inter-block corridor pivot beta(c'). The coarse straight path c uses beta(c), once, and no other selected corridor pivot. For x in B(c_-), the translated middle path [x,x'] has x'=x+L eta e_mu. It crosses exactly the corridor from B(c_-) to B(c_+); its only possible selected pivot is beta(c). It uses that pivot exactly when the d-1 transverse coordinates of x equal those of y. There are exactly L such x, with all L allowed longitudinal offsets. This incidence statement counts occurrences on periodic lifts; it is not an assumption that a long coarse contour is a single independent fine link.

Consequently row c of the actual physical mean depends on the selected fine variable beta(c) alone among ALL selected corridor pivots, at EVERY admitted background, not only at identity. No row c' distinct from c depends on beta(c). For (0.12), endpoint group means also remain independent of every corridor pivot because each is a function only of the endpoint paths within one block. We do not require a new inversion axiom for that group mean: keep the actual endpoint factors in (0.12) as defined. Thus the block derivative restricted to the original selected pivots is row diagonal. This is a geometric dependency statement, not yet invertibility of its diagonal blocks.

EXACT NONFLAT DIAGONAL BLOCK FOR BOTH FIXED DEFINITIONS. Write one chosen row in its own original formula as

 M_c(U)=exp(S_c) C_c,
 S_c=sum_alpha omega_alpha Log L_alpha,
 L_alpha=A_alpha T_x B_alpha C_c^-1.

Here C_c=U(c), T_x=U([x,x']), and A_alpha,B_alpha are the actual endpoint factors independent of the pivot. For (0.4), alpha=(x,Gamma,Gamma'), omega=L^-d/(|G(c_-,x)| |G(c_+,x')|), A=U(Gamma), B=U(-Gamma'). For (0.12), alpha=x, omega=L^-d and A,B are the actual averaged endpoint contours. In both cases sum_alpha omega=1. The original branch must be smooth and Lie(G)-valued on the actual real/unitary data, and exp(S_c) and the mean remain the declared physical quantities.

Let beta=beta(c) have the parent-to-child physical orientation of c and let rho=dot U_beta U_beta^-1; if its representative is reversed use rho_(beta^-1)=-Ad_(U_beta^-1)rho_beta and invert data consistently. Let R_c be the ordered fine background product in c strictly BEFORE beta. Let R_alpha be the product A_alpha followed by the prefix in T_x strictly BEFORE beta, when that middle path hits beta. Let chi_alpha be 1 for a hit and 0 otherwise; the term chi Ad_R is defined as zero when there is no hit, so no undefined prefix is used.

The logarithmic velocity of C_c is Ad_(R_c)rho. The logarithmic velocity of the open product A_alpha T_x B_alpha is chi_alpha Ad_(R_alpha)rho. Therefore

 dot L_alpha L_alpha^-1 = [chi_alpha Ad_(R_alpha)-Ad_(L_alpha)Ad_(R_c)]rho.

For a group element Z on the actual branch define ell_Z(B)=DLog_Z[B Z]; for a Lie-algebra element S define dexp_S(B)=integral_0^1 Ad_(exp(tS))B dt. These are the actual finite matrix differentials, not assigned norm bounds. In a genuine local log chart ell_Z=dexp_(Log Z)^-1; no existence of that inverse is claimed outside the admitted chart. The exact diagonal row derivative, in the explicit velocity convention dot U U^-1, is

 A_c(U)=dexp_(S_c) sum_alpha omega_alpha ell_(L_alpha)
       [chi_alpha Ad_(R_alpha)-Ad_(L_alpha)Ad_(R_c)]
       + Ad_(exp S_c)Ad_(R_c),

meaning dot M_c M_c^-1=A_c(U)rho for a variation supported on beta(c). The derivative of the final C_c is retained: losing it would change the answer. This formula differentiates either chosen original mean separately. It does not replace M_fix by the old native relative mean. Matrix/group/target velocities and order are explicit; no complex-Hermitian adjoint is substituted for a real-metric transpose.

FLAT CALIBRATION AND NORMALIZED Q. At the identity reference, all endpoint and prefix factors, L_alpha and C_c are I, S_c=0, and ell_I=dexp_0=I. The formula reduces to

 A_c(I)=[sum_alpha omega_alpha(chi_alpha-1)+1]I_g
       =(L/L^d)I_g=L^(1-d)I_g.

The endpoint-family weights sum to1 separately at each x; the middle-path hit count is L for both definitions. Thus the physical selected-pivot derivative is exactly delta_(c,c') L^(1-d)I, NOT I, L^-d I, or L I in group velocities. This is only a calibration at identity, not replacement of the actual physical U0 by I, and not a uniform nonflat estimate. For d=4,L=13 it is 1/2197 per Lie direction.

At a fixed nonflat reference define the actual physical relative constraint R(A)=Log[M_fix(exp(i eta A)U0) M_fix(U0)^-1]/i on its admitted chart. Its derivative is eta P A, where P is the physical group-velocity derivative above (the real Hermitian and anti-Hermitian conventions are related by multiplication by i). If the normalized coarse potential is R/(L eta), its linear operator is Q=P/L. Equivalently, at unit fine spacing the unnormalized relative coarse log is L Q A plus nonlinear terms, the convention in CMP109 (2.4)/(2.10). At flat, Q_(c,beta(c'))=delta_(c,c') L^-d I, hence 1/28561 for d=4,L=13.

If each ACTUAL diagonal A_c(U0) is invertible, define h_piv only on beta(c) by (h_piv B)_beta(c)=A_c(U0)^-1 B_c. Then P h_piv=I and LQ h_piv=I. At flat h_piv=L^(d-1)I on the pivot, 2197 for d4,L13. This identifies the pointwise normalization of the source's sparse h from its inverse coefficient definition. It does not identify h_piv with a minimizing-background derivative, variational H, normalized H_n, H1, a localized H_sigma, or the old propagator's Q without their actual averaging/metric/scale dictionary. A right-inverse identity alone does not supply their bounds or physical covariance.

RAW GROUP-CONSTRAINT ELIMINATION AND MEASURE FACTOR. At fixed original target V and all other active raw fine links fixed, each original active row depends on its own pivot beta(c) only. On a local branch where all A_c at the solutions are invertible, the group delta may be eliminated in these pivot variables. With the same normalized group Haar/delta on original fine links and targets, the local factor is

 product_(c in I) |det_(real Lie basis) A_c(U_solution)|^-1,

with a sum over distinct admitted regular roots if there is more than one branch, retaining the actual pulled-back domain, all original weights and words. Any other original coarse row and exterior constraint remains ONCE; geometric row diagonality does not make its value a function solely of V0 without a separate full support check. No root, off-chart contribution or original normalizer is discarded. An actual inverse on the whole original cutoff is NOT proved merely by the flat coefficient or by this local root formula.

At identity the group factor per pivot is L^((d-1)r), r=dim G. In Lie-coordinate notation with W=exp(i a), dW=sigma_G(a) da and group delta delta_G(exp(i z))=sigma_G(0)^-1 delta_g(z) at z=0, the linear relative log is LQ a. Eliminating a pivot gives sigma_G(0)*sigma_G(0)^-1*L^-r*|det Q_beta|^-1=L^((d-1)r), consistently. If instead a=eta g0 B, the pivot Haar scaling (eta g0)^r cancels the target delta scaling (L eta g0)^-r, still leaving L^-r*L^(d r). Remaining free-variable powers and exponential densities do NOT cancel by this per-pivot check; they remain in the original measure/normalizer. Away from identity keep the full sigma and nonlinear linearization determinant, not only the group factor or a flat approximation. This computation does not assert a numerical formula for the source's complete z^(0), whose original normalizations and other factors must be retained.

The actual source linearizes A_old'=A_linear-h D(A_linear), then scales A_linear=g0 B and solves Q B=0 by B=C A_free. Thus the physical original raw field contains the nonlinear term exp(i[g0 C A_free-h D(g0 C A_free)]) in the unit-spacing notation, not just exp(i g0 C A_free). Its sigma, derivative determinant, selected-pivot factor, cutoff and root transports remain. The source reuses prime labels during these operations; no source prefactor discrepancy or historical E1/g1_ref version issue is resolved by changing those labels. No analytic continuation of a real absolute determinant is asserted as an analytic complex determinant without the original source orientation/branch construction.

WHY THESE PIVOTS ARE NOT AUTOMATICALLY FREE Y LINKS. In the same L13 geometry, c:0->13 e1 has physical beta:(6,0,...)->(7,0,...). This is a boundary between the centered physical blocks, but lies INSIDE the native anchored [0,12]^d block and on its canonical comb tree. The full gauge chart fixes Y_beta=U0_beta, even though original U_beta may be active and varying. This is compatible with the closed1753 correction: 'physical centered corridor boundary' and 'native anchored interior' are different assertions. No native point-ring countertest is repeated or upgraded to a physical sector realization.

Consequently one must not eliminate Y_beta as if it were an independent free Y coordinate, or identify its index with one of the source's already free A variables. The raw source pivot variation has an explicit pullback to residual q=(kappa,free Y), computed at fixed target/reference as follows. Let z_b=dot U_b U_b^-1 be supported on the actual raw pivot, and let C_z=dot U(Gamma_rz)U(Gamma_rz)^-1 be its ordered path-prefix sum. With P=U0(Gamma) fixed and k_U=P^-1 U(Gamma), set

 chi_z=dot k(z)k(z)^-1=Ad_(P_rz^-1) C_z.

Only paths containing the raw varied tree edge contribute; more generally the formula includes every actual oriented occurrence. For native h_z=Ad_P k(z), X_z=Log h_z,

 dot X_z=ell_(h_z)(Ad_P chi_z),
 dot A_r=sum_z L^-d dot X_z,
 gamma_r=-Ad_(g_r)dexp_(A_r)(dot A_r),
 alpha_z=dot u(z)u(z)^-1=Ad_(P^-1)gamma_r+Ad_(l_g(z))chi_z.

These are q variations at fixed U0, not the target variations at fixed k from1758; dropping dot k here would be incorrect. The residual coordinate velocities are dot kappa_s kappa_s^-1=chi_s at the actual component tops and

 dot Y_b Y_b^-1=alpha_(b_-)+Ad_(u(b_-))z_b-Ad_(Y_b)alpha_(b_+)

on free non-tree links. For the right-recentered coordinate w=Y U0^-1, its velocity is the same at fixed U0. Prescribed fine links have z=0 and retain their transported targets. Tree Y velocities vanish because the exact inverse enforces Y_e=U0_e. These formulas explicitly construct the raw-pivot direction in the q chart, not just the symbol (D_q Psi)^-1. Applying the original physical coarse derivative along it recovers A_c(U) in its own row and zero in every other selected row, by the chain rule and the exact support calculation.

One may therefore retain the joint q representation or return to the original active raw group variables, a Haar-preserving full chart, and eliminate the ACTUAL beta pivots with the actual A_c determinant on admitted branches. This avoids the invalid uniformly invertible target block N from1758. It still does not permit a source-pivot determinant to be set to1 merely because the ambient fine Haar chart has factor1.

MARKED KERNEL AND LIMITS. Elimination substitutes each solution into the complete original density, domain and entire marked words. Crossing words are never split; wholly fine-prescribed words remain the original ordered V0 word once; open words and closed roots retain their actual frames. Complex finite polynomial sources are coefficientwise under original integrability. Derivatives of solutions, moving domains, frame/source factors and determinant densities need separate estimates before differentiating a physical integral. No positivity, nonzero denominator, connected-log expansion or history interchange follows from this coordinate step.

The exact nonflat A_c formula and row support are the new dictionary. Uniform invertibility on the ACTUAL original source/physical class, actual beta(c) outside F, the native-boundary B dictionary, K_C free-algebra correspondence, Landau section, Hsharp/source190 estimates, fixed beta_ref/g1_ref amplitude matching, P1 held issue, simultaneous component absorptions, off-chart control, normalization and histories remain unadmitted. Falsifiers include a selected pivot occurring in an endpoint contour or a different row, a wrong L^(1-d) count, a lost final-C derivative or adjoint, a false h normalization, deletion of fixed Y_beta, a missing dot k, or replacement of the original cutoff/mean/background to obtain a favorable determinant. This is one unfinished physical-coordinate calculation, not a new paper or a claim that a premise list is a physical theorem.
